description: Verdicts on the rule transducer's outputs, the judge the lattice needs where the single reference cannot decide (harness/lattice.py). `right`, `stiff` and `wrong` judge one specific output of one corpus sentence: right is natural Japanese that says what the English says; stiff is grammatical and faithful but not how it is said — better than a wrong output or a refusal, worse than natural Japanese; wrong is an output whose meaning is lost or changed, or whose Japanese is ill-formed. Plain against polite does not matter unless the sentence holds a clue that contradicts the form chosen, which is then wrong as an agreement error is; the wrong one of あげる / くれる / もらう is wrong in the same way. A stiff or wrong verdict names its cause, by which the frontier groups them. `input_ungrammatical` marks a corpus line whose English is not standard, so that refusing it is the top of its chain. `judge` says who gave a verdict — a human or the model; the verdicts recorded before the field existed carry none. The hook demands a verdict whenever an unjudged output changes or disappears; each unjudged output shown (old, new or both) gets a verdict, and a verdict is permanent.
